policy: The detailed catalog was curated by section membership, so a work can reach it because a chapter discusses it rather than because it demonstrates self-evolution. An entry listed here was checked against its own abstract and fails the inclusion criteria in docs/METHODOLOGY.md: it implements no self-evolving system, or its subject falls outside an agent changing its own output, model, scaffold, updater, or criterion. Removing an entry never removes a work the manuscript cites; active citations are always retained.

arxiv:2606.15096.title: VGPT-RSI for RH-Adjacent Formal Progress
arxiv:2606.15096.evidence: The abstract applies a system whose name contains Recursive Self-Improvement to two Riemann-Hypothesis certification tasks and reports Coq- and Arb-checked boundary certificates. It describes no update to an output, model, scaffold, updater, or criterion, so the RSI label is the system's name rather than a demonstrated mechanism. The curated note had already flagged the mechanism as unverifiable.

arxiv:2605.28512.title: On Compositional Learning Behaviours in Formal Mathematics
arxiv:2605.28512.evidence: The paper proposes the S2B-LM benchmark and cross-evaluates ten Lean 4 provers with a causal activation analysis. It measures a capability that self-evolving agents need without implementing self-evolution. The curated note reached the same conclusion: not a self-evolution implementation.

arxiv:2603.09405.title: YOLO-NAS-Bench: A Surrogate Benchmark with Self-Evolving Predictors
arxiv:2603.09405.evidence: A surrogate benchmark for YOLO architecture search. Its self-evolving mechanism retrains a LightGBM accuracy predictor on architectures the predictor itself selected, which is ordinary model retraining inside a NAS pipeline rather than an agent changing its own output, model, scaffold, updater, or criterion.

arxiv:2506.05109.title: Position: Truly Self-Improving Agents Require Intrinsic Metacognitive Learning
arxiv:2506.05109.evidence: A position paper that proposes a three-part conceptual framework and surveys how existing agents rely on extrinsic, human-designed improvement loops. It argues for a research direction and implements nothing.

arxiv:2606.01861.title: A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms
arxiv:2606.01861.evidence: A theoretical analysis of when a prover-conjecturer self-play system grows its proved-theorem set exponentially, given assumptions about a theorem graph. It characterises self-improvement rather than demonstrating a system that self-evolves.

arxiv:1905.10985.title: AI-GAs: AI-Generating Algorithms, an Alternate Paradigm for Producing General Artificial Intelligence
arxiv:1905.10985.evidence: A paradigm paper setting out the three pillars of AI-generating algorithms. The curated note already recorded that it implements no criterion-rewriting loop and forms a conceptual agenda.
